items.m03s3q4: Overall, visitor numbers at the Science Museum rose steadily over the ten years, whereas both the Art Gallery and the History Museum declined. The Science Museum overtook the Art Gallery in the middle of the period and the History Museum stayed the least visited.
items.m03s3q5: Overall, the share of coal fell sharply between 2000 and 2020, while wind and solar grew from a very small source to one of the largest. Natural gas became the leading source by 2020, and nuclear and hydro remained almost the same.
items.m03ckq8: Overall, teenagers spent the most time on social media and gaming, and both activities fell with age. Streaming video was similar in every age group, at about 12 to 15 hours a week, so it was the main activity for people aged 30 and over.
items.m04s3q5: Visitors to the Science Museum climbed from just over 400 thousand in 2010 to nearly 760 thousand in 2020.
items.m04s3q6: Teenagers spent 21 hours a week on social media, more than three times the 6 hours spent by people over 50.
items.m04ckq8: The share of coal fell from 48% in 2000 to 18% in 2020, less than half of its earlier level.
items.m06s3q7: The Science Museum began the period with around 420 thousand visitors in 2010, far fewer than the Art Gallery's 610 thousand. Its numbers then rose steadily and in 2014 it overtook the Art Gallery, with 570 thousand against 560 thousand. By 2020 it had reached 760 thousand, almost double its starting figure, because science became more popular with families.
items.m07s3q7: German teachers were the best paid, with a starting salary of 62000 dollars which rose to 81000 after 15 years. Thai teachers earned by far the least, at 9000 and 17000 dollars respectively, so a new German teacher earned almost seven times as much as a Thai one. Japanese and Korean salaries were similar, starting at 31000 and 33000 dollars.
items.m08s3q7: Overall, the recycling of glass is a cyclical process with eight stages. It starts when used bottles are collected at a bottle bank and ends when the new bottles are filled and delivered to shops, where the cycle begins again.
items.m09s3q7: Overall, the centre of Riverside changed from an industrial and commercial area into a residential and leisure area. The factory was replaced by apartments and traffic was moved out of the centre onto a new ring road, while the river, the park and the bus station remained in the same place.
items.m10s3q7: Finland had by far the highest consumption, at 21 cups per person per week. Italy and Brazil followed with 14 and 12 cups respectively, while Japan drank only 8 cups. Thailand consumed the least, at just 5 cups a week, which was less than a quarter of the Finnish figure.

plan.big: Science Museum went up a lot, Art Gallery and History Museum went down, Science became the most popular after 2014

slots.what: the number of visitors, in thousands, to three different museums in a European city
slots.groupB: the Art Gallery and the History Museum
slots.feature: the Science Museum became the most popular museum after 2014

p-line-museums.text:
The line graph gives information about the number of visitors (in thousands) to three different museums in a European city from 2010 to 2020.

Overall, the number of visitors to the Science Museum increased a lot, but the Art Gallery and the History Museum both decreased. The Science Museum became the most popular after 2014, and the History Museum was the lowest in every year.

In 2010, the Science Museum had 420 thousand visitors. This number rose to 570 thousand in 2014 and 710 thousand in 2018. In 2020 it reaches the highest point at 760 thousand visitors, which was almost two times higher than in 2010, maybe because science is more interesting for young people.

On the other hand, the Art Gallery was the most popular in 2010 with 610 thousand visitors, but it fell to 560 thousand in 2014 and 520 thousand in 2020. The History Museum also went down from 380 thousand in 2010 to 260 thousand in 2020, with a small rise in 2018.

Overall, the Science Museum increased a lot, but the Art Gallery and the History Museum both decreased, and the Science Museum became the most popular after 2014.

The Science Museum had 420 thousand visitors in 2010. It rose to 570 thousand in 2014 and 760 thousand in 2020, which was the highest number.

On the other hand, the Art Gallery fell from 610 thousand in 2010 to 520 thousand in 2020. The History Museum was the lowest in every year and went down from 380 thousand to 260 thousand.

slots.contrast: social media and gaming went down a lot with age, but streaming video was similar for all ages
slots.figA: 21 hours for 13–17 and only 6 hours for people over 50
slots.figB: between 12 and 15 hours for all groups
slots.exception: streaming video, which was the most popular activity for people over 30

p-bar-screentime.text:
The bar chart gives information about the average number of hours per week that people of four different age groups in one country spent on social media, streaming video and gaming in 2023.

Overall, the youngest group spent the most time on social media and gaming, and both went down a lot with age. However, streaming video was similar for all ages and was the most popular activity for people over 30.

People aged 13–17 spent 21 hours on social media, which was more than the 18 hours of the 18–29 group. The 30–49 group spent 11 hours and people over 50 only 6 hours because they are busy with work. Gaming was also highest for teenagers, at 12 hours, and it falls to only 1 hour for people over 50.

Streaming video was different. The 18–29 group watched the most at 15 hours, and the 30–49 group watched the least at 12 hours. For the over-50s, streaming at 13 hours was more than social media and gaming together.

plan.big: a man-made cycle with eight stages, from the bottle bank to the shops; first four prepare old glass, last four make new bottles

slots.product: how glass bottles are recycled and made into new bottles
slots.start: used bottles in a bottle bank
slots.end: new bottles delivered to the shops
slots.st1: used bottles are collected in a bottle bank and transported by lorry to the recycling plant
slots.st2: the bottles are washed with high-pressure water
slots.st3: they are sorted by colour and crushed into small pieces called cullet
slots.st4: is melted in a furnace at 600 to 800 degrees with new raw materials
slots.st5: the hot glass is moulded into new bottles
slots.st6: the bottles are filled and delivered to the shops, and the process starts again

p-proc-glass.text:
The diagram shows how glass bottles are recycled in eight steps.

Overall, this is a man-made cycle with eight stages. It starts when people put used bottles in a bottle bank and it finishes when new bottles are sent to the shops. The first four stages prepare the old glass and the last four stages make the new bottles.

First, used bottles are collected in a bottle bank. Then they are transported by lorry to the recycling plant. At the plant, the bottles are washed with high-pressure water and after that they are sorted by colour, which is clear, green and brown. Next, the glass is crushed into small pieces called cullet.

In the second part, the cullet is melted in a furnace at 600 to 800 degrees, and new raw materials are added. Then the hot glass is moulded into new bottles. Finally, the bottles are filled and delivered to the shops, and the process starts again. This is a very good system because it saves energy.

plan.big: the town became more modern with more buildings; old buildings replaced in the same places; river and temple the same

slots.place: the centre of a small town in the north-east of Thailand
slots.change: became more modern and had more buildings
slots.where2: south-east, on most of the rice fields
slots.extended: the main road was made wider and now has four lanes

p-map-thai-town.text:
The maps show the centre of a small Thai town in the north-east in 2005 and in 2025.

Overall, the town centre became more modern and had more buildings in 2025. Most of the old buildings were replaced by new buildings in the same places, and a hospital was built on the rice fields. However, the river and the temple stayed the same.

In the north of the main road, the wet market in the west was changed to a covered market, and the open field next to it became a car park. The temple in the north-east corner did not change. The main road was also made wider to four lanes.

In the south, the wooden houses in the south-west were demolished and townhouses were built there instead. A new hospital was built on most of the rice fields in the south-east, so the rice fields are much smaller now, which is bad for farmers. Also, the ferry crossing on the river was replaced by a bridge.

plan.big: smartphones increased very quickly and basic phones decreased in the same way; the lines crossed between 2013 and 2016

slots.what: the percentage of teenagers in one country that had a smartphone and the percentage that had a basic mobile phone
slots.groupA: the percentage of teenagers with a smartphone
slots.groupB: the percentage with a basic phone
slots.feature: the two lines crossed between 2013 and 2016, and in 2025 almost all teenagers had a smartphone

p-line-phones.text:
The graph shows the percentage of teenagers in one country that had a smartphone and the percentage that had a basic mobile phone from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, the percentage of teenagers with a smartphone increased very quickly, while the percentage with a basic phone decreased in the same way. The two lines crossed between 2013 and 2016, and in 2025 almost all teenagers had a smartphone and only a few had a basic phone.

In 2010, only 10% of teenagers owned a smartphone. The figure rose to 30% in 2013 and 60% in 2016, which was higher than basic phones for the first time. After that, it continues to grow to 80% in 2019, 90% in 2022 and 95% in 2025.

Basic phones were the opposite. In 2010, 80% of teenagers had one, but it dropped to 65% in 2013 and 40% in 2016. Then it fell to 20% in 2019 and 10% in 2022, and in 2025 only 5% of teenagers still used a basic phone.

mocks.mock1:
The line graph shows the percentage of homes with internet access in four countries, Sweden, Japan, Thailand and Kenya, from 2005 to 2025.

Overall, internet access increased in all four countries. Sweden and Japan were high during the whole period and were almost the same in 2025, while Thailand had the biggest increase. Kenya grew a lot but was still the lowest in every year.

Sweden had the highest figure, which rose from 70% in 2005 to 92% in 2015 and 97% in 2025. Japan started at 60% in 2005, but it increased to 88% in 2015 and 95% in 2025, so it was very close to Sweden.

In contrast, only 12% of households in Thailand had internet in 2005. This figure rose quickly to 52% in 2015 and 88% in 2025. Kenya was only 2% in 2005 and it rises to 35% in 2020 and 52% in 2025, but this was still much lower than the other countries.
mocks.mock2:
The table shows the amount of rice that four countries produced in 2000, 2010 and 2020, in million tonnes.

Overall, China produced the most rice in all three years, but India had the biggest increase. Vietnam and Thailand produced much less than China and India, and Thailand was the only country where production went down between 2010 and 2020.

China's production increased from 188 million tonnes in 2000 to 197 million in 2010 and 212 million in 2020. India produced 127 million tonnes in 2000, which was much lower than China, but it rose to 144 million in 2010 and 178 million in 2020.

The other two countries were much smaller. Vietnam grew slowly from 32 million tonnes in 2000 to 40 million in 2010 and 43 million in 2020. Thailand rose from 26 million to 36 million in 2010, but then it decreases to 30 million in 2020, so it was the smallest producer.
mocks.mock3:
The two maps show a secondary school campus now and the changes that are planned for the future.

Overall, the plan will add more buildings and more green space, but the sports field will become much smaller. The library and the car park will move to new places, while the main building and the road will stay the same.

Now, the main building is in the north-west corner, next to the road, and the car park is in the north-east. In the centre, the library and the canteen are next to each other, with an open ground to the east, and the sports field is in the south.

In the plan, the car park will be changed into a garden, and a new car park will be built on the open ground. The canteen will be extended to the west into the library's place, and a new library will be built in the south-west. As a result, the sports field will be reduced to half of its size in the south-east.
